title: World Affairs and History
lines: General Knowledge in USAT-A uses stable facts only. For world affairs this means international organisations (founding year, headquarters, purpose), major treaties and events of world history, and famous firsts. Questions never ask about current leaders or the latest news, so learn facts that will stay true.
- Founded on 24 October 1945 (United Nations Day), after the Second World War, replacing the League of Nations (1920, Geneva). Headquarters: New York. Pakistan joined on 30 September 1947.

- Six principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council (inactive since 1994), International Court of Justice (The Hague), and Secretariat, headed by the Secretary-General.
- The Security Council has 15 members: 5 permanent members with a veto (China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States) and 10 elected for two-year terms.
| IMF and World Bank | 1944 (Bretton Woods) | Washington, D.C.
| 1215 | Magna Carta sealed in England, limiting the king's power
| 1498 | Vasco da Gama reaches India by sea
| 1914–1918 | First World War; ended by the Treaty of Versailles (1919)
| 1939–1945 | Second World War; atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1945)
| 1948 | Universal Declaration of Human Rights adopted by the UN
| Peace of Westphalia | 1648 | ended the Thirty Years' War; basis of the modern state system
| Treaty of Versailles | 1919 | peace terms with Germany after the First World War
| Geneva Conventions | 1949 | protect the wounded, prisoners and civilians in war
| Indus Waters Treaty | 1960 | shared the Indus rivers between Pakistan and India
| Tashkent Declaration | 1966 | Pakistan-India agreement after the 1965 war
| Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty | 1968 | limits the spread of nuclear weapons
| Simla Agreement | 1972 | Pakistan-India agreement after the 1971 war
| Kyoto Protocol | 1997 | first binding targets for greenhouse gases
| Paris Agreement | 2015 | climate pact to keep warming well below 2 °C
| People on the Moon | Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, Apollo 11, 1969
| Ascent of Mount Everest | Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, 1953
- Pakistan won the Cricket World Cup in 1992 and the ICC T20 World Cup in 2009. These are historical facts and will stay true.
> The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency is in  (A) Geneva  (B) Vienna  (C) Paris  (D) New York
> B. Geneva is the tempting choice because many UN bodies are there, but the IAEA, like OPEC, is in Vienna.
> Which country is NOT a permanent member of the Security Council?  (A) France  (B) China  (C) Germany  (D) Russia
> C. The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA.
! The League of Nations was based in Geneva; the UN is in New York.
! SAARC was founded at Dhaka, but its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
! The IMF and World Bank were planned at Bretton Woods in 1944 and are both in Washington, D.C.
- UN: 24 October 1945, New York, Security Council of 15 with 5 vetoes.
- Geneva: WHO, ILO, WTO, Red Cross. Vienna: IAEA, OPEC. Paris: UNESCO. Rome: FAO.
- OIC Jeddah 1969; SAARC 1985; ECO Tehran; ASEAN Jakarta.
